findings.problem: Two proofs use the same argument. Both cancel the epi `K.map (toNormalizedChainComplex R)`. Both then run a roughly 13-step explicit `calc` that pushes the square through the projection, using three facts. The first is the naturality of the projection (`toNondegComplex_nondegComplexMap`). The second is the comparison square for the projection (`..._hom_app`). The third is a square for the all-simplex comparison, either `h` or `hA`. Each step carries a hand-written `congrArg (fun k : ... ↦ ...)` and a type ascription, so the two proofs total about 60 lines of near-identical diagram chasing, once for `Φ` with `Ψ` and once for `θ`.
findings.proposed_change: Extract one lemma of this shape. Take an arbitrary chain map `u : K.obj (S.chainComplex R) ⟶ P` and arbitrary maps `v w` out of `P` and out of the matching target. Then deduce an equality of maps out of `K.obj (S.normalizedChainComplex R)` from the corresponding equality after precomposing with `K.map (S.toNormalizedChainComplex R)`. Concretely, state it for `m₁ m₂ : K.obj (S.normalizedChainComplex R) ⟶ Q` with `K.map (S.toNormalizedChainComplex R) ≫ m₁ = K.map (S.toNormalizedChainComplex R) ≫ m₂ → m₁ = m₂`. This is `cancel_epi` and is available from the split epi. Then prove each chase with `simp only [Category.assoc]` and `rw [reassoc_of% hqΦ, ...]` instead of the `calc` blocks. The first proof could also be rewritten as the special case of the second with `L = M`. The chase `K.map q ≫ (m ≫ b) = a ≫ q' ≫ n` should be factored as: `K.map q ≫ F ≫ b_T = a_S ≫ G_T` follows from the three squares. Pass the three squares as arguments.
findings.benefit: Cuts about 60 lines of duplicated `calc` and `congrArg` scaffolding to a few `rw` lines per use. The mathematical content, which is that the comparison commutes with the projection and everything else is naturality, becomes visible. Any change to the comparison definition needs one edit rather than two.
